rationales: Corals are living marine animals, not the preserved remains of extinct organisms.
Fossils are preserved remains or traces of organisms from the past.
A coral reef is a structure formed by corals, not the remains of extinct organisms in general.
Endangered describes a species at risk of extinction, not its remains.
Roots mainly absorb water and minerals and anchor the plant.
Stems support the plant and transport materials.
Flowers are the reproductive organs of flowering plants.
Leaves mainly carry out photosynthesis and gas exchange.
“Mala” means “bad,” as in the term malaria, meaning bad air.
“Good” is not the meaning of “mala.”
“Air” is not the meaning of “mala.”
“Water” is not the meaning of “mala.”
Taxonomy deals chiefly with identifying, naming, and classifying organisms.
Systematics studies organismal diversity and relationships, including evolutionary history.
Genetics studies genes and heredity, not classification and evolutionary history as a whole.
Ecology studies relationships between organisms and their environment.
Plant cells generally have a cell wall.
Fungal cells have a cell wall, typically containing chitin.
Bacterial cells generally have a cell wall, although some exceptions exist.
Animal cells lack a cell wall.
Chloroplasts are green plastids containing chlorophyll.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids.
Chromoplasts contain pigments that give them colour.
Lipids are fats and related molecules, not a type of plastid.
Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
“Pharagomoplast” is not the term for cytoplasmic division.
Phagocytosis is the engulfing of particles by a cell.
Metaphase follows prophase and involves chromosomes lining up at the cell equator.
Anaphase follows metaphase and involves sister chromatids separating.
Interphase is the period between cell divisions, not the reversal of prophase.
Telophase reverses many events of prophase as the nuclei reform and chromosomes decondense.
Cellulose is a carbohydrate, not the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
Glucose is a simple sugar, not the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
Lipids are not the usual chemical nature of enzymes.
Most enzymes are proteins.
Lysosomes digest materials within cells and are not the main site of aerobic respiration.
The cytoskeleton provides structural support and is not the main site of aerobic respiration.
Mitochondria are the main site of aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells.
Plastids are not the site of aerobic respiration.
Ribs contain red bone marrow, where red blood cells are produced in adults.
The spleen mainly filters blood and removes old red blood cells.
The liver is a major site of blood-cell formation before birth, not the usual adult site.
The lungs exchange gases and do not produce red blood cells.
Anatomy studies the structure of organisms and their parts.
Genetics studies genes and their role in inheritance.
Taxonomy concerns the naming and classification of organisms.
Histology studies tissues.
Sixteen is the textbook figure for the number of bio-elements in nature.
Fourteen is not the stated textbook figure for bio-elements in nature.
Twelve is not the stated textbook figure for bio-elements in nature.
Ten is not the stated textbook figure for bio-elements in nature.
A. F. A. King proposed a mosquito-related explanation of malaria but was not the French army physician in 1878.
Ronald Ross later demonstrated the role of mosquitoes in malaria transmission.
Laveran was the French army physician who discovered the malaria parasite in 1878.
Mendel is known for foundational work on inheritance, not malaria.
Mushrooms are fungi.
Mushrooms are not animals.
Mushrooms are not members of Monera.
Mushrooms are not protists.
